passages.title: Receiving Onesimus as a brother tests love within an unequal relationship
passages.summary: Paul, a prisoner, writes with Timothy to Philemon and the assembly in his house. Paul thanks God for Philemon’s love and faith. He could command, but he appeals out of love. He appeals for Onesimus, who became his child during his imprisonment. Paul sends him back and calls him his own heart. He asks Philemon to receive him as a beloved brother, more than a slave. Paul will repay anything Onesimus owes. He asks for a guest room and sends greetings.
passages.uncertainty: No exact location is assigned to unnamed or heavenly settings.

lds.text: Why does receiving Onesimus as Paul himself make partnership costly?

contextNote.title: Receiving Onesimus as a brother tests love within an unequal relationship
contextNote.text: Verse 8 says Paul could command Philemon and chooses to appeal. Verse 16 asks that Onesimus be received as a beloved brother. Verse 17 puts the request in terms of partnership. If Philemon counts Paul a partner, he must receive Onesimus as he would Paul. That puts the returning servant in the apostle’s place at the door. Verse 18 removes the money objection: Paul will pay what is owed. Verse 21 adds that Paul expects Philemon to do even more than he asks.

words.label: Apostles
words.meaning: People sent out with a message. In the Gospels the word names twelve whom Jesus chose.

words.label: Saints
words.meaning: People set apart as holy. In the letters the word means the believers in a place.

words.label: Assembly
words.meaning: A gathering of people. In the New Testament letters it means a group of believers. Many translations say “church.”
